interactions.label: In the six-link chain of HAI transmission, which link is the PRIMARY target for

params.question: In the six-link chain of HAI transmission, which link is the PRIMARY target for most hospital infection control interventions?

answers.text: Infectious agent — by developing new antibiotics to eliminate resistant organisms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While new antibiotics help treat infections, they do not break the chain of transmission. Antibiotic stewardship addresses the agent link but is not the primary infection control strategy.

answers.text: Mode of transmission — by interrupting contact, droplet, and airborne routes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Hand hygiene, PPE, environmental cleaning, isolation rooms, and safe injection practices all target the mode of transmission, making it the most actionable intervention point in the chain.

answers.text: Susceptible host — by vaccinating all admitted patients

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Vaccination does reduce host susceptibility (e.g. hepatitis B for HCWs), but many HAI patients are immunocompromised or post-surgical — their susceptibility cannot be fully modified by vaccination alone.

answers.text: Portal of entry — by removing all invasive devices as soon as possible

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Prompt device removal is an important bundle element (e.g. early catheter removal for CAUTI prevention), but it addresses only one portal of entry and is not the broadest infection control strategy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the six links of the chain. The narration emphasised that the mode of transmission is 'where most infection control efforts focus,' because hand hygiene, PPE, isolation, and cleaning all target this link.
Well done. The mode of transmission is the most actionable link because multiple evidence-based strategies — hand hygiene, PPE, isolation, environmental cleaning — all converge on breaking this link.

interactions.label: By what mechanism did the NDM-1 carbapenemase gene spread between DIFFERENT bact

params.question: By what mechanism did the NDM-1 carbapenemase gene spread between DIFFERENT bacterial species in hospitals worldwide?

answers.text: Clonal spread — the same resistant organism passing from patient to patient on healthcare workers' hands

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Clonal spread transmits an entire organism between patients but does not transfer genes between different species. NDM-1 jumped across species barriers, which requires a different mechanism.

answers.text: Chromosomal point mutations arising under antibiotic selection pressure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Chromosomal mutations can generate new resistance within a single species but do not transfer resistance genes between different bacterial species.

answers.text: Horizontal gene transfer via plasmids carrying the resistance gene

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. NDM-1, first identified in New Delhi, is carried on plasmids — mobile DNA elements that can transfer between entirely different bacterial species, explaining its rapid global dissemination.

answers.text: Intrinsic impermeability encoded in the bacterial chromosome from birth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Intrinsic resistance (e.g. Pseudomonas's natural impermeability) is built into the organism's own chromosome. NDM-1 is acquired resistance, not intrinsic, and it moves between species.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall that the narration distinguished two hospital spread mechanisms: clonal spread (same organism, patient to patient) and horizontal gene transfer (genes moving between different species via plasmids). NDM-1 uses the latter.

Exactly. Plasmid-mediated horizontal gene transfer allows resistance genes like NDM-1 to hop between entirely different bacterial species — a key reason why carbapenem resistance has become a global crisis.

interactions.label: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to your hospital. Wh

params.question: A patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to your hospital. Which set of precautions and specific requirements are correct for this patient?

answers.text: Droplet precautions — surgical mask and one-metre spatial separation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Droplet precautions are for organisms like influenza that travel in larger droplets over short distances. TB spreads via much smaller droplet nuclei that remain airborne and travel further, requiring stricter measures.

answers.text: Contact precautions — single room, gloves and gown on entry, dedicated equipment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Contact precautions target organisms spread by touch, such as MRSA and C. difficile. TB is not primarily spread by contact; it is transmitted through airborne droplet nuclei.

answers.text: Airborne precautions — negative-pressure room, N95 respirator, and closed door

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. TB spreads via tiny droplet nuclei that float and linger in the air. A negative-pressure room prevents contaminated air from escaping, an N95 respirator filters the small particles, and the door must remain closed.

answers.text: Standard precautions alone — hand hygiene, gloves, and respiratory hygiene are sufficient

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Standard precautions apply to all patients but are insufficient for TB. Transmission-based precautions must be added on top of standard precautions when a specific pathogen is identified or suspected.

overallFeedback.feedback: The narration classified TB under airborne precautions — the strictest tier — because TB spreads via tiny droplet nuclei. These require a negative-pressure room, an N95 respirator, and a closed door.

Correct. Airborne precautions are the strictest tier, reserved for pathogens like TB, measles, and varicella that spread through tiny droplet nuclei requiring negative-pressure isolation and N95 respirators.

interactions.label: You have finished caring for a patient on contact precautions and are about to r

params.question: You have finished caring for a patient on contact precautions and are about to remove your PPE. Which item should you remove FIRST during doffing, and why?

answers.text: Mask or respirator — because it is closest to your airway and poses the greatest inhalation risk

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The mask is actually removed LAST during doffing, handled only by the ties or ear loops. Removing it first would require contaminated gloved hands near your face, increasing infection risk.

answers.text: Gown — because it covers the largest surface area and has the most contamination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The gown is removed after the gloves and eye protection. It is rolled inside-out to contain the contaminated exterior, but this step comes later in the doffing sequence.

answers.text: Gloves — because the outer glove surface carries the most contact contamination

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Gloves are removed first using the glove-into-glove technique, since their outer surface has had the most direct contact with the patient and contaminated surfaces. Hand hygiene follows immediately before touching any other PPE.

answers.text: Eye protection — because removing it first gives better visibility for the remaining steps

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Eye protection is removed after gloves (by the earpieces only). Removing it first with contaminated gloves would transfer organisms to the face. Visibility is not the determining factor — contamination sequence is.

overallFeedback.feedback: Recall the doffing order: gloves FIRST (most contaminated outer surface, glove-into-glove technique), then hand hygiene, then eye protection by earpieces, then gown rolled inside-out, then mask by ties, then final hand hygiene.
Exactly right. The doffing sequence — gloves, hand hygiene, eye protection, gown, mask, hand hygiene — is designed so that clean hands never touch contaminated surfaces.

interactions.label: A nurse has just given an intramuscular injection. Under the Biomedical Waste Ma

params.question: A nurse has just given an intramuscular injection. Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules 2016, into which container should the used needle and syringe be discarded?

answers.text: Yellow bag — since the needle is contaminated with blood

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Yellow bags are for anatomical waste (Category 1) and soiled waste like blood-soaked dressings (Category 2). Although needles are blood-contaminated, their sharp nature requires a puncture-proof container to prevent needle-stick injuries.

answers.text: White, translucent, puncture-proof container (sharps bin)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Sharps — needles, syringes, blades, and broken glass — are Category 3 and must go into white, puncture-proof containers. They are then autoclaved or dry-heat treated, shredded, and encapsulated. Remember: needles must never be recapped before disposal.

answers.text: Blue bag — with other single-use clinical items

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Blue bags are reserved for discarded or expired medicines (Category 4, non-cytotoxic). Sharps have specific puncture-proof disposal requirements that a standard bag cannot provide.

answers.text: Black bag — with general hospital solid waste

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Black bags are for non-contaminated general solid waste like packaging and food waste. Used needles are both contaminated and hazardous, requiring Category 3 sharps disposal.

overallFeedback.feedback: Under BMW Rules 2016, sharps (needles, syringes, blades, broken glass) are Category 3 and must go into white, translucent, puncture-proof containers — not colour-coded bags, which cannot prevent needle-stick injuries.
Correct. Category 3 sharps always go in white, puncture-proof containers — the physical hazard (needle-stick injury) dictates the container type, regardless of the biological contamination present.

interactions.label: Routine environmental surveillance of hospital water, food, and air is a high-yi

params.question: Routine environmental surveillance of hospital water, food, and air is a high-yield activity and should be performed continuously in all hospital areas to prevent healthcare-associated infections.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually false. The narration explained that routine environmental surveillance has low yield under normal conditions. Instead, targeted surveillance — triggered by an outbreak or new construction work — is the standard approach, directing resources to where the contamination risk is real.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Routine surveillance has low yield when nothing unusual is happening. Targeted surveillance, triggered by specific events such as an outbreak or new construction, is the recommended approach because it focuses resources where contamination risk is actually elevated.
